A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NatADiff work, with the same title and authors. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet attack-generation experiments, transferability and image-quality results, boundary-guidance ablations, and defence evaluations.

after.justification: V2 reports original ImageNet and Oxford Pets experiments, expanded ablations and defence evaluations, runtime measurements, and a human label-preservation study.

M1.justification: Equation 10 changes cosine-similarity target selection from argmin to argmax, correcting the formula toward the already-stated most-similar-class rule. Boundary guidance, normalized augmented gradients, time travel and adaptive retries remain unchanged. Algorithm 2 still uses argmin, so this documented correction does not establish a corresponding implementation change.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates ImageNet classification, using ImageNet-Val and ImageNet-A as reference distributions. V2 retains this coverage and adds Oxford Pets classification in Appendix I, testing finer distinctions between pet breeds that require subtler adversarial features. This materially extends evaluation beyond the original object-category setting.

E2.justification: V1 compares NatADiff with PGD, AutoAttack and adversarial classifier guidance, called AdvClass. V2 adds NCF, DiffAttack and ACA to both the main comparison and defence evaluation (Tables 1 and 10). AdvClass also gains comparisons using Inception-v3 and ViT-H surrogates, whereas v1 reports it only with ResNet-50.

E3.justification: ASR changes from matching the attack-selected adversarial label in v1 Section 4.1 to counting any misclassification in v2 Section 5.1, including randomly targeted attacks. The main evaluation expands from five to nine victim models, and the clean comparison baseline changes from SD1.5 samples to an ImageNet-compatible dataset. V2 also introduces NIQE, BRISQUE and TReS metrics and distinct protocols for prompt/guidance ablations, Oxford Pets and human evaluation.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's boundary-strength sweep and illustrative component comparison, v2 adds quantitative classifier-augmentation ablation, eight prompt variants, guidance-strength and gradient-trajectory analyses, UMAP/t-SNE feature probes, and human label-preservation and failure-case analyses. Defence testing is expanded. Conversely, v1 Appendix I's separate AutoAttack-implementation and model-family transferability investigation is removed; the original component illustration and boundary-strength examples are retained elsewhere.

E5.justification: V2 Figures 8–10 introduce mean gradient trajectories with bands representing plus/minus one standard deviation; v1 contains no corresponding dispersion reporting. This is a limited addition: principal performance tables remain point estimates, and the PDFs do not establish increased independent runs or multi-seed evaluation.

E6.justification: Main, ablation and defence results are revised and expanded. For targeted ResNet-50 NatADiff, reported IS/FID-Val/FID-A change from 37.2/42.8/53.8 in v1 Table 2 to 26.0/66.5/77.3 in v2 Table 1, without explaining the recalculation. New results include Oxford Pets and human judgments of 91% true class, 7% adversarial class and 2% neither. Revised ASR values cannot be interpreted as same-setting gains because its definition changes.

T1.justification: V2 Section 2 adds formal definitions of unconstrained, constrained and natural adversarial sets using an oracle classifier, together with their inclusion relation. Equation 10 corrects the cosine-similarity extremum. The conditional-forward and score-model theorems and proofs are substantially retained, moving from v1 Appendix H to v2 Appendix P rather than constituting new theory.

C1.justification: The central boundary-guidance and transferability contributions remain. V2 explicitly qualifies comparable attack success as white-box performance and narrows the introduction/conclusion's natural-error alignment claim to comparison with adversarial classifier guidance, replacing v1's broader assertions of close resemblance to naturally occurring errors.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies v1's general advantage for untargeted attacks with a ViT-H exception and explicitly explains that artifacts inflate targeted ViT-H ASR. It adds substantive interpretations of augmentation quality tradeoffs, guidance strength, feature projections, Oxford Pets generalization and DiffPure failures, including increased NCF transferability. The human study also qualifies label preservation with observed failures. Appendix A nevertheless retains the now-inconsistent ImageNet-only limitation.

D1.justification: V2 adds a reproducibility section stating that code and configuration files accompany the supplementary material, expanded parameter tables for ImageNet and Oxford Pets, model-source information, and the human study's selected class list. Runtime documentation expands from approximately 90 seconds per sample to a comparison reporting 103.1 seconds for NatADiff. Conversely, v1's explicit corner-crop/horizontal-flip recipe and image/latent dimensions disappear. Actual supplementary code availability cannot be verified from these PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 broadens positioning beyond the earlier emphasis on GANs and AdvClass by explaining NatADiff's relationship to NCF's color restrictions, DiffAttack's source-image constraints and ACA's semantic editing. It adds literature on these comparisons, additional architectures, perceptual metrics, manifold visualization and human annotation, while shortening the GAN discussion and removing several associated references. ACA was already cited in v1; its evaluated and discussed role expands.

P1.justification: Preliminaries move from the methodology into a standalone section before related work, and the experimental setup and results narrative undergo substantial rewriting. V2 distinguishes surrogate from victim models and reorganizes the appendices, splitting parameter selection from ablations, moving proofs to the end and adding a contents page. These changes exceed simple renumbering or appended scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns the main table to combine ASR and image quality, group results by surrogate and victim architecture, and highlight rankings in color. Defence and boundary-ablation tables are also consolidated. It adds comparison images, gradient plots, manifold plots and failure examples. V1 Figure 2 moves to v2 Figure 5; v1 Figure 3 is simplified in the main text while its detailed version survives as v2 Figure 14.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central contribution through relevant unconstrained-attack baselines, component-specific ablations, Oxford Pets evaluation and direct human evidence of label preservation. Its explicit acknowledgment of artifact-inflated ViT-H results also improves interpretation. These gains outweigh the loss of target-specific ASR reporting and remaining reporting inconsistencies. The restricted human study and unexplained image-quality score revisions still limit conclusions, but the evidential basis is considerably stronger than v1's.
